sections.title: Eligibility and preparation
sections.text:
Eligibility for your route [Standing rule]
The General Mathematics BS-entry PhD explicitly accepts a mathematics or closely related bachelor’s degree.
The catalog lists a 3.0 undergraduate GPA and permits holistic exceptions to GPA/test thresholds. An
international UChicago mathematics graduate is academically eligible to apply, subject to those standards. [s1]
[s3] [s6]
Before submission [Standing rule]
Select the BS-entry General Mathematics PhD in ApplyUTA, arrange three letters, prepare all college records
and any requested academic/research statement, and resolve tests or waivers. Ask the department for any
fee-waiver code before submission. F-1 transfer eligibility and financial certification are needed for the later
I-20 process. [s1] [s4] [s5] [s9]
Adviser contact [Standing rule]
No signed supervisor commitment is listed. Research fits include noncommutative algebraic geometry,
Lie/superalgebra representations and commutative/homological algebra. Faculty interaction can contribute to
holistic admission review, but current supervision capacity must be confirmed. [s6] [s10] [s11]
Portal workflow [Standing rule]
MyMav shows application status and a to-do list for missing materials; allow 5-7 business days for processing. A
letter-specific receipt display or automatic receipt email was not separately established. A complete
application normally takes 3-5 weeks for a decision. [s5]
Cycle verification [Standing rule]
Current 2026-27 catalog and standing department/central pages were checked November 5, 2026. Specific Fall
2027 funding amounts and final closing/acceptance dates remain unconfirmed. [s1] [s2] [s3] [s6]

sections.title: Deadlines by stage
sections.text:
Academic application [Standing rule]
Central doctoral fall priority is February 1, but the mathematics funding priority is January 1 and should govern
a funded application. Central catalog guidance prefers international credentials 120 days before enrollment; it
is not a substitute for the earlier mathematics priority. A final Fall 2027 mathematics closing date was not
established. [s1] [s3] [s4]
Funding consideration; Reference receipt; Test-score receipt; Supporting documents [Standing rule]
Complete the admission application, including required records, letters and scores, by January 1 for full GTA
consideration. Review may continue until positions fill. No separate later reference, score or document
deadline is published; incomplete files cannot be evaluated. These are standing dates. [s1] [s2]

Accepting an offer [Unresolved]
A specific Fall 2027 admission/funding acceptance deadline was not established in the reviewed official pages.
Obtain it from the offer; do not equate February 1 application priority with a commitment deadline. [s1] [s2]

sections.title: English and GRE
sections.text:
English requirement [Standing rule]
Without an exemption: TOEFL new-scale overall 4, with published section targets writing 4.5 and
speaking/reading/listening 4; former TOEFL overall 79 with writing 22, speaking 21, reading 20 and listening
16; IELTS 6.5 or Duolingo 100. Send official scores to ETS code 6013 where applicable. [s4]
UChicago English exemption [Standing rule]
Holding a bachelor’s or master’s from an accredited US institution exempts admission English testing. The
catalog also exempts a US bachelor’s degree from the separate international teaching-assistant English
demonstration requirement. Whether the admission waiver can be processed while the UChicago degree is still
pending is not established. Otherwise GTA certification can require speaking assessment/training; Duolingo
admission acceptance does not itself establish GTA certification. [s3] [s4]
GRE General [Standing rule]
The current 2026-27 BS-entry catalog lists General GRE thresholds of verbal 143 and quantitative 155 for
unconditional admission, while allowing a holistic exception when GPA and/or GRE criteria are unmet. No
blanket mathematics GRE waiver was found; treat it as required unless the department approves otherwise.
[s6]
GRE Mathematics [Unresolved]
No Mathematics Subject GRE requirement or preference was established. The catalog’s numerical GRE
thresholds concern the General test and must not be misread as a subject-test requirement. [s6]

sections.text:
Transcripts and degree records [Conflict]
Provide records of all undergraduate/graduate college work. Current central instructions permit unofficial
uploads for review, followed by official transcripts after admission or when available; older catalog language
asks for official records with credentials. If you have non-US college records, the international page now
requires FCSA review with a separate $90 processing fee; a UChicago-only record does not trigger that
foreign-record rule. [s3] [s4] [s5]

sections.title: Recommendation letters
sections.text:
Number and type [Standing rule]
At least three letters from people familiar with academic and/or professional work. Enter referee contact details
in the application; letters are submitted through an emailed link. [s1] [s6]
Scholarship references [Standing rule]
The admission application itself serves as the GTA application; no separate standard assistantship reference or
essay is listed. Other scholarship/fellowship requirements need individual confirmation. [s1] [s2]
What sends the invitation; Before versus after submission [Unresolved]
The department says contact information entered in the application leads to an email invitation. It does not

explicitly identify whether saving the details or submitting the application triggers the email; confirm in
ApplyUTA. [s1]
Receipt confirmation [Standing rule]
MyMav shows application status and a to-do list for missing materials; allow 5-7 business days for processing. A
letter-specific receipt display or automatic receipt email was not separately established. A complete
application normally takes 3-5 weeks for a decision. [s5]
Updating and reusing letters [Unresolved]
No public mathematics/central rule for replacing submitted letters or reusing them across cycles was
established in the reviewed application guidance. Ask admissions before assuming either is possible. [s1] [s5]

sections.title: Funding and fees
sections.text:
Amount and coverage [Standing rule]
The live mathematics GTA page advertises $25,666.56 over twelve months ($2,138.88 monthly), 100% tuition
benefit and year-round student health coverage. A student opting out of summer work keeps health coverage
but receives no summer stipend. The page is undated and is not a guaranteed Fall 2027 offer. [s2]
Years of support [Unresolved]
A multiyear guarantee was not established. Stipends rise with degree progress, with promotions at the start of
a semester. Confirm the initial appointment length and renewal conditions in the offer. [s2]
International eligibility [Standing rule]
International students can receive the same graduate tuition benefit as eligible domestic appointees. The
international-services fee is not covered. The department gives funding preference to unconditionally admitted
PhD-bound students; not every eligible admitted student is funded. [s1] [s8]
Conditions and duties [Standing rule]
A GTA normally works 20 hours per week and takes nine credits in fall and spring. Duties can include grading,
labs or teaching. Central tuition-benefit rules include enrollment/GPA requirements; clarify summer credits and
any post-candidacy reduction with the Graduate School. [s2] [s8]
Extra funding application [Standing rule]
The admission application itself serves as the GTA application; no separate standard assistantship reference or
essay is listed. Other scholarship/fellowship requirements need individual confirmation. [s1] [s2]
Other funding routes [Unresolved]
The mathematics aid page lists research assistantships, RTG/bridge opportunities and departmental named
awards including Bernfeld, McCarley, Ray and Mathematics Academic Excellence funds. Their current

availability, F-1 eligibility, separate statements and deadlines are not established; do not assume federally
restricted bridge awards are international-accessible. [s7]
Application fee [Standing rule]
The international graduate application fee is $90 and nonrefundable. Non-US transcript review, if applicable,
carries an additional $90 FCSA fee. [s3] [s4]
Fee waiver [Standing rule]
The current fee-waiver page directs graduate applicants to their academic department for a code before
submitting. It does not guarantee a code or publish mathematics-specific eligibility. The generic undergraduate
hardship form says graduate applicants are ineligible, so use the departmental code route rather than that
form. [s9]

The live department gives January 1 funding priority, earlier than central February 1. Current central
admissions allows unofficial review transcripts while catalog wording requests official records. The current
departmental fee-waiver-code route differs from the undergraduate form’s exclusion of graduate applicants.

sections.title: Potential advisers and recent research
sections.text:
Noncommutative algebraic geometry
Michaela Vancliff
Quadratic algebras, quantum projective spaces, point schemes and Ore extensions. [s10] [s11] [s12]
Listed on official departmental faculty pages; availability to supervise new PhD students is not published.
Research evidence: 2026 · The point scheme of quadratic algebras that are Ore extensions of a twist of the polynomial ring
Recent research evidence; verify supervision availability separately.
Representation theory
Dimitar Grantcharov
Lie-algebra and Lie-superalgebra representations; recent work studies simple sl(2) modules free of finite rank
over a Cartan enveloping algebra. [s10] [s11] [s13]
Listed on official departmental faculty pages; availability to supervise new PhD students is not published.
Research evidence: 2026 · A family of simple U(h)-free modules of rank 2 over sl(2)
Recent research evidence; verify supervision availability separately.
Commutative / homological algebra
David A. Jorgensen
Commutative algebra, cohomology, complete intersections and triangulated categories. [s10] [s11] [s14]
Listed on official departmental faculty pages; availability to supervise new PhD students is not published.
